- A public Azure Firewall named FW1  
- A route table named RT1 associated with Subnet1  
- A rule in RT1 that routes `0.0.0.0/0` to FW1  
  
After you deploy 10 servers running Windows Server to Subnet1, you find that none of the virtual machines are activated.  
  
You need to make sure that the virtual machines can be activated.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: On FW1, configure a DNAT rule for port 1688
Add an internet route to RT1 for the Azure Key Management Service (KMS).
To Subnet1, associate a network security group (NSG) that allows outbound access to port 1688.

questions.explanation:
Azure Windows virtual machines activate through the Azure Key Management Service (KMS) endpoint on port 1688. A `0.0.0.0/0` route to a firewall forces that activation traffic through the firewall. For forced-tunneling configurations, a more-specific user-defined route for the Azure KMS IP addresses must send that traffic directly to the Internet so the VMs can reach KMS.

**Learn more:** [Use Azure custom routes to enable KMS activation with forced tunneling](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/azure/virtual-machines/windows/custom-routes-enable-kms-activation) · [Event 8198, error 0xC0020017 or 0x8007139F when activating Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/licensing-and-activation/activation-event-8198-error-0xc0020017-0x8007139f-kms-contact-failure)

questions.domain: Design and implement private access to Azure services
questions.question:
You need to use Traffic Analytics to monitor application usage for deployments on Azure virtual machines.  
  
Which Azure Network Watcher feature should you implement first?
questions.explanation:
Traffic Analytics analyzes Azure Network Watcher flow logs to provide insights into traffic patterns, including the most-communicating application protocols. NSG flow logs record IP traffic processed through a network security group and provide the flow data required for this analysis.\
\
**Learn more:** [Traffic Analytics Overview - Azure Network Watcher](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/traffic-analytics) · [Create, change, enable, disable, or delete NSG flow logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/nsg-flow-logs-manage)

questions.domain: Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure App Service app that uses the URL https://www.contoso.com.  
  
You need to configure a custom domain on Azure Front Door for www.contoso.com. The custom domain must use a certificate from an allowed certification authority (CA).  
  
What should you include in the solution?

options.text: an enterprise application in Azure Active Directory (Azure AD)

questions.explanation:
To use a custom domain with a certificate issued by an allowed CA on Azure Front Door, you must bring your own certificate (BYOC) rather than use the Front Door managed certificate. Azure Front Door requires that customer-provided TLS/SSL certificates be stored in Azure Key Vault, from which Front Door retrieves the certificate to enable HTTPS on the custom domain. This satisfies the requirement to use a certificate from a specific allowed CA, since Front Door's managed certificates come only from a Microsoft-selected CA.

**Learn more:** [Configure HTTPS on a Front Door custom domain using your own certificate](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/frontdoor/front-door-custom-domain-https)

questions.domain: Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that includes a web app named App1 and an Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) on Azure Front Door instance named FD1. FD1 manages traffic for App1.  
  
You need to ensure that traffic is automatically detected and blocked when an IP address sends abnormally high volumes of traffic to App1. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you include in the solution?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Front Door WAF rate-limiting rule sets a request threshold per client IP address for a defined time window and blocks traffic after that threshold is exceeded. This automatically mitigates abnormally high traffic without maintaining a static IP block list.

**Learn more:** [WAF Rate Limiting for Azure Front Door](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/web-application-firewall/afds/waf-front-door-rate-limit)

You have an Azure subscription that includes a virtual network.  
  
You plan to deploy an Azure VPN gateway and 90 Site-to-Site VPN connections. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Ensure the Site-to-Site VPN connections remain available if an Azure datacenter fails.  
- Minimize costs.  
  
Which gateway SKU should you specify?
questions.explanation:
A zone-redundant VPN Gateway SKU is required for resilience to an Azure datacenter failure. VpnGw4AZ supports zone redundancy and up to 100 Site-to-Site/VNet-to-VNet tunnels, satisfying the 90-connection requirement. VpnGw5AZ also has sufficient capacity but is a higher SKU, so VpnGw4AZ minimizes cost among the listed qualifying options.

**Learn more:** [About gateway SKUs - Azure VPN Gateway](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/about-gateway-skus) · [Reliability in Azure Virtual Network Gateways](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/about-zone-redundant-vnet-gateways)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing a virtual network named VNet1. VNet1 has a subnet mask of `/24`.  
  
You plan to deploy an Azure Application Gateway with the following configuration:  
  
- Public endpoints: 1  
- Private endpoints: 1  
- Minimum instances: 1  
- Maximum instances: 10  
  
You need to configure the address space for the Application Gateway subnet. The solution must minimize the number of IP addresses assigned to that subnet.  
  
What is the minimum number of assignable IP addresses needed?
questions.explanation:
Azure Application Gateway requires one private IP address in its subnet for each gateway instance, based on the maximum instance count, and one additional private IP address for a private frontend configuration. A public frontend uses a public IP resource rather than an address from the Application Gateway subnet. Thus, 10 maximum instances plus one private frontend require 11 assignable IP addresses.

**Learn more:** [Azure Application Gateway infrastructure configuration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/application-gateway/configuration-infrastructure) · [Azure Application Gateway frontend IP address configuration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/application-gateway/configuration-frontend-ip)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your on-premises network includes a DNS server named Server1.  
  
You have an Azure subscription containing the resources displayed in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783847168150-q31zrk1w.png)  
  
The on-premises network connects to VNet1 by using a Site-to-Site (S2S) VPN.  
  
You need to make sure that Server1 can resolve the DNS name of storage1. The solution must minimize cost and administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: an Azure virtual machine that hosts a DNS service

questions.explanation:
An Azure DNS Private Resolver inbound endpoint lets an on-premises DNS server conditionally forward private-endpoint DNS queries over the VPN to Azure DNS, which resolves the linked private DNS zone and returns the private endpoint address. It is a managed service and avoids deploying and maintaining a DNS-forwarder virtual machine.

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Create a private endpoint DNS infrastructure with Azure Private Resolver for an on-premises workload](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/private-link/tutorial-dns-on-premises-private-resolver) · [Azure DNS Private Resolver endpoints and rulesets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/private-resolver-endpoints-rulesets)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has offices in London, Tokyo, and New York. The company has a web app named App1 with the Azure Traffic Manager profile shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783813348219-d8576r2y.jpg)  
  
In Asia, you plan to deploy an additional endpoint that will host an updated version of App1.  
  
You need to route 10 percent of traffic from the Tokyo office to the new endpoint during testing. What should you configure in Traffic Manager?
questions.explanation:
A Geographic Traffic Manager profile can route Tokyo-originated requests to an Asia-specific nested endpoint, while a Weighted child profile distributes that Asia traffic between the existing and updated App1 endpoints. Assigning relative weights of 90 and 10 in the child profile sends approximately 10 percent of that traffic to the updated endpoint. The Geographic parent contains three endpoints—East US, UK South, and the nested Asia profile—and the Weighted child contains the two Asia app endpoints, for five endpoints across two profiles.

**Learn more:** [Nested Traffic Manager profiles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/traffic-manager/traffic-manager-nested-profiles) · [Traffic Manager routing methods](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/traffic-manager/traffic-manager-routing-methods)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing the public IPv4 addresses shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783809605461-bp4ozl8z.png)  
  
You plan to create a load balancer named **LB1** with these settings:  
  
- Name: LB1  
- Location: West US  
- Type: Public  
- SKU: Standard  
  
Which public IPv4 address(es) can LB1 use?

options.text: IP1, IP3, IP4, and IP5 only
IP1, IP2, IP3, IP4, and IP5

questions.explanation:
A public Standard Load Balancer requires a Standard SKU public IP address, and a regional load balancer frontend public IP must be deployed in the same region. IP3 is the only address with the Standard SKU in West US; IP5 is in West US 2, and IP1, IP2, and IP4 use the Basic SKU.

**Learn more:** [Azure Load Balancer SKUs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/load-balancer/skus) · [Azure Load Balancer portal settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/load-balancer/manage)

questions.question:
You need to grant access to `storage2`. The solution must satisfy the PaaS networking requirements and the business requirements.  
  
Which connectivity method should you use?
questions.explanation:
An Azure private endpoint gives a virtual network a private IP address for a specific Azure Storage resource and carries the connection through Azure Private Link on the Microsoft backbone. This provides private connectivity to the PaaS resource, unlike a service endpoint, which accesses the service's public endpoint.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use private endpoints for Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-private-endpoints) · [What is Azure Private Link?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/private-link/private-link-overview)

questions.domain: Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing a virtual machine named VM1, a virtual network interface card (NIC) named NIC1, and a Basic SKU public IP address named IP1. NIC1 is attached to VM1, and IP1 is associated with NIC1.  
  
You need to upgrade IP1 to the Standard SKU.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Create a new NIC for VMI.

questions.explanation:
A Basic SKU public IP must be disassociated from its attached resource before it can be upgraded to the Standard SKU. Because IP1 is associated with NIC1, disassociate IP1 from NIC1; detaching the NIC or stopping the virtual machine is unnecessary.

**Learn more:** [Upgrade Basic Public IP Address to Standard SKU in Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/ip-services/public-ip-basic-upgrade-guidance) · [Upgrade public IP addresses attached to VM from Basic to Standard](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/ip-services/public-ip-upgrade-vm)

questions.domain: Design and implement application delivery services
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription linked to an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant named `contoso.onmicrosoft.com`. The subscription includes the following resources:  
  
- An Azure App Service app named App1  
- An Azure DNS zone named `contoso.com`  
- An Azure private DNS zone named `private.contoso.com`  
- A virtual network named Vnet1  
  
You create a private endpoint for App1. Azure DNS automatically registers the endpoint record.  
  
You need to give a developer the name registered in Azure DNS for the private endpoint.  
  
What should you provide?
questions.explanation:
Azure App Service private endpoints use the `privatelink.azurewebsites.net` private DNS zone. The endpoint record is named after the app within that zone, so App1 is registered as `app1.privatelink.azurewebsites.net`.

**Learn more:** [Use private endpoints for Azure App Service apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-private-endpoint)

questions.domain: Design and implement private access to Azure services
questions.question:
You are designing the IP addressing for subnets within Azure virtual networks.  
  
Which resource type requires IP addresses in the subnets?

options.text: Azure DDoS Protection for virtual networks

questions.explanation:
An internal load balancer requires a private frontend IP address from a subnet in its virtual network. Service endpoints and service endpoint policies provide connectivity and traffic-filtering configuration, and Azure DDoS Protection does not allocate a subnet IP address.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Load Balancer portal settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/load-balancer/manage) · [Azure virtual network service endpoints](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-service-endpoints-overview)

questions.domain: Design and implement application delivery services
questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure App Service web app named WebApp1 and an Azure Front Door profile named FDProfile1. FDProfile1 forwards requests sent to https://www.contoso.com to WebApp1.  
  
You need to ensure that only requests sent to https://www.contoso.com/users/* are forwarded to WebApp1.  
  
What should you modify in FDProfile1?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Front Door route matches incoming requests by domain and path pattern, and the route specifies the origin group to which matching traffic is forwarded. Setting the route pattern to `/users/*` limits forwarding to requests under that path.\
\
**Learn more:** [How requests get matched to a route configuration - Azure Front Door](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/frontdoor/front-door-route-matching)

questions.domain: Design and implement Azure network security services
questions.question:
You have a hybrid environment that uses ExpressRoute to link an on-premises network with Azure.  
  
You need to periodically record the connection’s uptime and latency by using an Azure virtual machine and an on-premises virtual machine.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Connection Monitor provides ongoing, end-to-end monitoring between Azure deployments and on-premises locations over ExpressRoute. It records connectivity and performance data, including availability and latency, using Azure and on-premises monitoring endpoints.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure Connection Monitor for Azure ExpressRoute](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/expressroute/connection-monitor-overview) · [Connection Monitor overview - Azure Network Watcher](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/connection-monitor-overview)

questions.domain: Design and implement Azure network security services

options.text: From NSG1, modify the priority of Rule2.
From each virtual machine, associate the network interface to ASG1.
From Subnet1, create a subnet delegation.
From ASG1, modify the role assignments.

questions.explanation:
An application security group is a logical grouping of network interfaces. An NSG rule that specifies ASG1 as its destination applies to only the network interfaces assigned to ASG1. Associating each App1 virtual machine’s NIC with ASG1 makes the existing Rule2 manage inbound SFTP traffic for all three VMs without separate IP-based rules.

**Learn more:** [Network security groups and application security groups](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/networking/design-guide/network-application-security-groups) · [Azure Application Security Groups Overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/vi-vn/azure/virtual-network/application-security-groups?cid=kerryherger)

You have an on-premises datacenter named Site1 that includes a firewall named FW1. FW1 is connected to the internet.  
  
You have an Azure subscription containing the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783884342196-sly45x3x.png)  
  
You plan to connect Site1 to Hub1 by using a site-to-site connection.  
  
You need to configure the site-to-site connection to FW1.  
  
What should you create in VWAN1?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Virtual WAN VPN site represents an on-premises location and holds the endpoint details for its on-premises VPN device. Creating a VPN site for Site1 enables FW1 to be connected to the Hub1 site-to-site VPN gateway. Virtual network connections instead attach Azure virtual networks to a virtual hub.

**Learn more:** [Create a site-to-site connection using Azure Virtual WAN](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-wan/virtual-wan-site-to-site-portal) · [About virtual hub settings in Azure Virtual WAN](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-wan/hub-settings)

You have an Azure subscription that contains the resources displayed in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783884816736-3mexw33h.png)  
  
You need to configure FW1 to filter traffic originating from VNet1 that targets the FQDN of SQLDB1.  
  
Which rule type should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Firewall application rules support filtering Azure SQL Database traffic by SQL FQDN when SQL connectivity mode is set to Proxy. Proxy-mode SQL FQDN filtering uses an application rule; network rules are the alternative when SQL uses Redirect mode.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure Azure Firewall application rules with SQL FQDNs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall/sql-fqdn-filtering) · [Use FQDN filtering in Azure Firewall network rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall/fqdn-filtering-network-rules)

Set IPsec / IKE policy to Custom.

questions.explanation:
To connect a route-based Azure VPN gateway to a policy-based on-premises VPN device, the connection must use policy-based traffic selectors. Azure requires a complete custom IPsec/IKE policy when policy-based traffic selectors are enabled; therefore, the IPsec/IKE policy must be set to Custom.

**Learn more:** [Connect a VPN gateway to multiple on-premises policy-based VPN devices](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/vpn-gateway-connect-multiple-policybased-rm-ps)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure virtual network and an on-premises datacenter.  
  
You plan to establish a Site-to-Site VPN connection between the datacenter and the virtual network.  
  
Which two resources should be included in the plan? Each correct answer is part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
A Site-to-Site VPN uses a virtual network gateway as the Azure VPN endpoint and a local network gateway to represent the on-premises VPN device and its address prefixes. Only the virtual network gateway appears among the supplied choices; the required local network gateway is missing. An on-premises data gateway is not a VPN gateway resource.

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Create a site-to-site VPN connection in the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/tutorial-site-to-site-portal) · [Configure a Site-to-Site VPN for Azure Files](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/files/storage-files-configure-s2s-vpn)

You have an Azure subscription containing a virtual network named VNet1. VNet1 includes the following subnets:  
  
- AzureFirewallSubnet  
- GatewaySubnet  
- Subnet1  
- Subnet2

Subnet2 is delegated to the Microsoft.Web/serverfarms service.  
  
The subscription contains the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783841176153-ud1nbph3.png)  
  
You need to deploy an Azure application gateway named AG1 that is integrated with an Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF). AG1 will publish VMSS1.  
  
To which subnet should AG1 be connected?
questions.explanation:
Azure Application Gateway requires a dedicated subnet that cannot contain other resource types. GatewaySubnet is reserved for gateway resources, AzureFirewallSubnet is dedicated to Azure Firewall, Subnet2 is delegated to Microsoft.Web/serverfarms, and Subnet1 already contains the virtual machine scale set. Subnet3 is the available dedicated subnet.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an application named App1 that listens for inbound requests on a preconfigured set of 50 TCP and UDP ports.  
  
You deploy App1 to 10 Azure virtual machines.  
  
You need to implement load balancing for App1 across every virtual machine. The solution must minimize the number of load-balancing rules.  
  
What should the solution include?

options.text: Azure Application Gateway V2 that has multiple listeners
Azure Standard Load Balancer that has Floating IP enabled
Azure Standard Load Balancer that has high availability (HA) ports enabled
Azure Application Gateway v2 that has multiple site hosting enabled

questions.explanation:
An Azure Standard Load Balancer HA ports rule is configured with protocol **All** and port **0**, allowing one rule to load-balance TCP and UDP flows on all ports of an internal Standard Load Balancer. This minimizes rules for an application using many TCP and UDP ports.

**Learn more:** [Azure Load Balancer components — High Availability Ports](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/load-balancer/components?view=azureml-api-2)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Front Door instance named FD1 that is protected by Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF).  
  
FD1 uses the frontend host name `app1.contoso.com` to provide access to Azure web apps hosted in the East US Azure region and the West US Azure region.  
  
You need to configure FD1 to block requests to `app1.contoso.com` originating from every country except the United States.  
  
What should you include in the WAF policy?

options.text: a custom rule that uses a match rule
a custom rule that uses a rate limit rule

questions.explanation:
Azure Front Door WAF supports country-based access control through a custom match rule with a geographic match condition. The rule can match requests whose client location is not the United States and apply the Block action. Rate-limit rules are for request-rate thresholds, while managed rule sets provide predefined threat protection rather than a custom country restriction.

**Learn more:** [Geo-filtering on a domain for Azure Front Door](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/web-application-firewall/afds/waf-front-door-geo-filtering) · [Custom rules for Azure Web Application Firewall on Azure Front Door](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/web-application-firewall/afds/waf-front-door-custom-rules)

All virtual machines are connected to VNet1.  
  
You need to ensure that the applications hosted on the virtual machines are accessible from the internet. The solution must ensure that the virtual machines share one public IP address.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
A public Azure Load Balancer uses one Internet-facing public frontend IP address and can distribute Layer 4 TCP traffic using rules for ports 443, 25, and 22 to the appropriate backend virtual machines. This supports HTTPS, SMTP, and SFTP through the shared public IP address.

**Learn more:** [Internet ingress: expose your application to the internet](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/networking/design-guide/internet-ingress) · [Manage a public IP address with a load balancer](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/ip-services/configure-public-ip-load-balancer)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You plan to deploy an Azure virtual network.  
  
You need to design the subnets.  
  
Which three resource types require a dedicated subnet? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
> **NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Azure Active Directory Domain Services (Azure AD DS)

questions.explanation:
Azure Bastion, Microsoft Entra Domain Services (Azure AD DS), Application Gateway v2, and VPN Gateway require dedicated subnets. Bastion uses the reserved `AzureBastionSubnet`; Domain Services must use a dedicated subnet; Application Gateway requires a subnet containing only Application Gateway resources; and VPN Gateway uses `GatewaySubnet`, where no other resources may be deployed. Azure Private Link does not inherently require a dedicated subnet. Thus, the listed choices contain four qualifying resources rather than three.

**Learn more:** [Azure Bastion configuration settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bastion/configuration-settings) · [Create a customized Microsoft Entra Domain Services managed domain](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/domain-services/tutorial-create-instance-advanced)

questions.question:
You have an Azure Private Link service named PL1 that uses an Azure Load Balancer named LB1.  
  
You need to make sure that PL1 supports a greater volume of outbound traffic.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Increase the number of frontend IP configurations for LB1.
Increase the number of NAT IP addresses assigned to PL1.
Deploy an Azure Application Gateway v2 instance to the source NAT subnet.
Redeploy LB1 with a different SKU.

questions.explanation:
Private Link Service NAT IP configurations provide source NAT for Private Link traffic. Each NAT IP address adds TCP ports and connection capacity; therefore, assigning additional NAT IP addresses to the Private Link service scales its outbound traffic capacity.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Private Link FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/private-link/private-link-faq) · [What is Azure Private Link service?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/private-link/private-link-service-overview)

questions.question:
You have an Azure Private Link service named PL1 that uses an Azure Load Balancer named LB1.  
  
You need to make sure that PL1 supports a greater volume of outbound traffic.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create an object replication rule for storage.
From storage1, select Secure transfer required.

questions.explanation:
An Azure subnet can have only one Azure Storage service-endpoint type associated with it. Microsoft.Storage is the regional endpoint, whereas Microsoft.Storage.Global provides cross-region connectivity. The existing Microsoft.Storage endpoint must therefore be deleted before the cross-region endpoint can be added for access to the RA-GRS secondary region.

**Learn more:** [Azure Storage firewall rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-network-security)

questions.question:
You have an on-premises datacenter and an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to deploy ExpressRoute FastPath.  
  
You need to create an ExpressRoute gateway. The solution must minimize downtime if a single Azure datacenter fails.  
  
Which SKU should you use?
questions.explanation:
ExpressRoute FastPath is supported by the Ultra Performance/ErGw3AZ gateway tier. ErGw3AZ is an availability zone-enabled, zone-redundant SKU, which provides resilience against the failure of a single Azure datacenter.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure ExpressRoute FastPath: Features, availability, and limitations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/expressroute/about-fastpath) · [Reliability in Azure Virtual Network Gateways](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/about-zone-redundant-vnet-gateways)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing 100 network security groups (NSGs).  
  
You need to ensure that the application of specific NSG rules is logged.  
  
Which type of log should you configure?
questions.explanation:
The application of specific NSG rules is captured by NSG diagnostic resource logs, which have two categories: Event (logs the NSG rules applied to a VM, based on MAC address, including rule name, direction, priority and allow/deny type) and Rule counter (how many times each rule is applied). Both are enabled through Diagnostic settings and are classified as Azure resource logs. NSG (or virtual network) flow logs are a different, Network Watcher feature that records the IP traffic flowing through the NSG rather than the rule application itself, and the flow-log note even states the source IP of communication isn't in the resource log. The activity log records control-plane operations (who changed the NSG), and 'audit log' isn't an NSG log type, so the correct choice is the Azure resource log.

**Learn more:** [Diagnostic resource logging for an NSG](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-nsg-manage-log)

questions.domain: Design and implement private access to Azure services
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have 10 on-premises networks connected by a third-party Software Defined Wide Area Network (SD-WAN) solution. You have an Azure subscription that contains five virtual networks.  
  
You plan to connect the Azure virtual networks and the on-premises networks by using Azure Virtual WAN with a single virtual WAN hub.  
  
You need to ensure that Azure Virtual WAN can function as a node in the third-party SD-WAN solution.  
  
What should you include in the solution?

options.text: An Azure Virtual WAN ExpressRoute gateway
A Site to site gateway (VPN gateway)
A Point to site gateway (User VPN gateway)

questions.explanation:
A Network Virtual Appliance deployed in an Azure Virtual WAN hub can serve as a third-party SD-WAN gateway. It terminates SD-WAN connectivity from on-premises networks and exchanges routes with the virtual WAN hub, enabling the hub to participate in the third-party SD-WAN solution.

**Learn more:** [How to create a Network Virtual Appliance in an Azure Virtual WAN hub](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-wan/how-to-nva-hub) · [Azure Virtual WAN partners, regions, and available locations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-wan/virtual-wan-locations-partners)

questions.domain: Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.question:
You are planning IP addressing for subnets within Azure virtual networks.  
  
Which resource type requires IP addresses in the subnets?

options.text: Azure DDoS Protection for virtual networks

questions.explanation:
A private endpoint is a network interface deployed into a virtual-network subnet and is assigned a private IP address from that subnet’s address range. NAT Gateway is associated with a subnet but uses configured public IP addresses for outbound connectivity; DDoS Protection and service endpoint policies do not consume subnet IP addresses.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage Azure private endpoints](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/private-link/manage-private-endpoint) · [Azure Virtual Network IP Services overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/ip-services/ip-services-overview)

questions.domain: Design and implement application delivery services
questions.question:
Solution: Configure a custom cookie and an exclusion rule.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
OWASP CRS rule 920300 blocks requests that lack an `Accept` header. A custom cookie and a cookie exclusion do not address the missing request header, so the WAF can continue to return HTTP 403. Azure WAF exclusions omit only the selected request attributes from evaluation; they do not alter unrelated request-header requirements.\
\
**Learn more:** [Web Application Firewall exclusion lists in Azure Application Gateway](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/web-application-firewall/ag/application-gateway-waf-configuration) · [Web Application Firewall CRS and DRS rule groups and rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/web-application-firewall/ag/application-gateway-crs-rulegroups-rules)

questions.domain: Design and implement Azure network security services
questions.question:
Solution: Create a WAF policy exclusion for request headers that contain `137.135.10.24`.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
`137.135.10.24` is the source client IP address, while the block is caused by OWASP CRS rule `920300` detecting a missing `Accept` request header. Application Gateway WAF exclusions omit selected request attributes, such as header values, from WAF evaluation; an exclusion for a header value containing that IP address does not address the missing-header rule and would not allow access from every IP address. [Microsoft Learn: Web Application Firewall exclusion lists](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/web-application-firewall/ag/application-gateway-waf-configuration)\
\
**Learn more:** [Web Application Firewall exclusion lists in Azure Application Gateway](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/web-application-firewall/ag/application-gateway-waf-configuration)

questions.domain: Design and implement application delivery services
questions.question:
Solution: You add a rewrite rule for the Host header.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
The request is blocked by WAF rule 920300 because its `Accept` header is missing. Rewriting the `Host` header does not affect that `Accept`-header rule or the WAF action, so it cannot make the URL accessible from any IP address.\
\
**Learn more:** [CRS and DRS rule groups and rules - Azure Web Application Firewall](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/web-application-firewall/ag/application-gateway-crs-rulegroups-rules)

questions.domain: Design and implement private access to Azure services
questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure Front Door named FD1. FD1 is configured as shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783884559782-h1rm6xox.png)  
  
You need to enable Azure Private Link for FD1.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Change Pricing Tier to Azure Front Door Premium.

questions.explanation:
Azure Front Door supports Private Link for origins only on the Premium tier. Because FD1 is currently on the Standard tier, it must be changed to Azure Front Door Premium before Private Link can be enabled.\
\
**Learn more:** [Secure your origin with Private Link in Azure Front Door Premium](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/frontdoor/private-link) · [Secure traffic to Azure Front Door origins](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/frontdoor/origin-security)

questions.domain: Design and implement private access to Azure services
questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure Front Door named FD1. FD1 is configured as shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783884559782-h1rm6xox.png)  
  
You need to enable Azure Private Link for FD1.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Modify the DNS server settings of Vnet1.
For FW1, configure custom DNS server.
On the on-premises DNS servers, configure forwarders that point to the frontend IP address of FW1.
On the on-premises DNS servers, configure forwarders that point to the Azure provided DNS service at 168.63.129.16.

questions.explanation:
Azure Firewall DNS proxy listens for DNS queries on port 53 and forwards them to its configured DNS resolver. An on-premises DNS server can use the firewall frontend IP as a conditional forwarder, allowing requests to traverse ExpressRoute and be resolved against the private DNS zone linked to the firewall virtual network. Azure-provided DNS at 168.63.129.16 is a virtual IP for resources within an Azure virtual network and is not a direct on-premises DNS-forwarder target.

**Learn more:** [Azure Firewall DNS settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall/dns-settings) · [Azure Private Endpoint DNS integration scenarios](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/private-link/private-endpoint-dns-integration)

questions.domain: Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company operates five offices. Every office has a firewall device and its own local internet connection. The offices are connected through a third-party SD-WAN.  
  
You have an Azure subscription that includes a virtual network named Vnet1. Vnet1 includes a virtual network gateway named Gateway1. Each office connects to Gateway1 by using a Site-to-Site VPN connection.  
  
You need to replace the third-party SD-WAN with Azure Virtual WAN.  
  
What should the solution include?

options.text: Create new Point-to-Site (P2S) VPN connections on the firewall devices.
Create an Azure Traffic Manager profile.

questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual WAN uses VPN sites and a VPN gateway deployed in a Virtual WAN hub for branch Site-to-Site connectivity. The existing virtual network gateway is therefore not needed in the replacement design and must be deleted after its Site-to-Site connection resources are removed. Point-to-Site VPN is intended for individual client connections, while Traffic Manager and active-active mode do not replace the branch VPN topology.

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Create site-to-site connections using Virtual WAN](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-wan/virtual-wan-site-to-site-portal) · [Delete a virtual network gateway using the portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/vpn-gateway-delete-vnet-gateway-portal)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have the Azure virtual networks shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783810107447-3xtwxrxf.jpg)  
  
You have the Azure resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783810114230-8x3qlcum.jpg)  
  
You need to use connection monitors in Azure Network Watcher to check latency between the resources.  
  
What is the minimum number of connection monitors that you need to create?
questions.explanation:
A Connection Monitor is a region-specific resource, and Azure VM source endpoints must be in the same region as the monitor. VM1 and VM3 can be monitored from one East US connection monitor, while VM2 requires a second monitor in UK West. A monitor can include multiple endpoints, and destination VMs can be selected from another region, so two monitors provide the required coverage.

**Learn more:** [Create a connection monitor using the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/connection-monitor-create-using-portal) · [Connection Monitor overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/connection-monitor-overview)

questions.domain: Design and implement application delivery services
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains four virtual networks named VNet1, VNet2, VNet3, and VNet4.  
  
You plan to deploy a hub-and-spoke topology by using virtual network peering.  
  
You need to configure VNet1 as the hub network. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Support transitive routing between spokes.  
- Maximize network throughput.  
  
What should you include in the solution?
questions.explanation:
Azure Firewall deployed in the hub can provide the transit data path between peered spokes when user-defined routes send spoke traffic to the firewall’s private IP address. This enables spoke-to-spoke routing despite nontransitive VNet peering and provides a scalable, high-throughput hub appliance.

**Learn more:** [Hub-and-spoke network topology - Azure Virtual Network](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/networking/design-guide/hub-spoke) · [Azure Firewall and traffic inspection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/networking/design-guide/azure-firewall)

questions.domain: Design and implement application delivery services
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Front Door instance with one frontend named Frontend1 and an Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) policy named Policy1. Policy1 redirects requests whose header contains "string1" to https://www.contoso.com/redirect1. Policy1 is associated with Frontend1.  
  
You need to configure additional redirection settings. Requests to Frontend1 with a header containing "string2" must be redirected to https:// www.contoso.com/redirect2.  
  
Which three actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Add a custom rule to Policy1.

questions.explanation:
A custom WAF match rule can evaluate a request header and apply a Redirect action. The rule must be added to Policy1, which is already associated with Frontend1, so the existing association enforces the new rule. Creating another association is not required for an already associated policy; therefore, only two listed actions are technically necessary.

questions.question:
You are planning IP addressing for subnets in Azure virtual networks.  
  
Which resource type requires IP addresses in the subnets?
questions.explanation:
An internal load balancer requires a private frontend IP address from a virtual network subnet. This frontend IP is the internal endpoint through which the load balancer receives traffic.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Load Balancer portal settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/load-balancer/manage)

questions.question:

Which resource type requires IP addresses in the subnets?
questions.explanation:
ExpressRoute Local provides connectivity only to the Azure region or regions near its ExpressRoute peering location and includes an Unlimited data plan. With both the on-premises datacenter and the East US peering location in Washington DC, and no resources outside East US, its local scope satisfies the requirement at lower cost than Standard, Premium, or ExpressRoute Direct.

questions.question:
You have an Azure Application Gateway named AppGW1 that load-balances requests to a web app named App1.  
  
You need to change the server variables in App1's response header.  
  
What should you configure on AppGW1?
questions.explanation:
Azure Application Gateway rewrite rules can add, remove, or update HTTP response headers. A rewrite action can use supported server variables as header values, so URL rewrite rules provide the required configuration.\
\
**Learn more:** [Rewrite HTTP headers and URL with Azure Application Gateway](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/application-gateway/rewrite-http-headers-url)

You have an Azure Application Gateway named AGW1 with a routing rule named Rule1. Rule 1 sends traffic for http://www.contoso.com to a backend pool named Pool1. Pool1 targets an Azure virtual machine scale set named VMSS1.  
  
You deploy an additional virtual machine scale set named VMSS2.  
  
You need to configure AGW1 so that all traffic for http://www.adatum.com is directed to VMSS2. The solution must ensure that requests for http://www.contoso.com continue to be directed to Pool1.  
  
Which three actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Host-based routing in Azure Application Gateway uses a multi-site listener configured for the incoming host name. A request-routing rule associates that listener with a backend pool, so VMSS2 must be placed in a new backend pool and a new rule must connect the www.adatum.com listener to that pool. Leaving the existing listener, Rule1, and Pool1 unchanged preserves routing for www.contoso.com.

**Learn more:** [Hosting multiple sites on Azure Application Gateway](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/application-gateway/multiple-site-overview) · [Azure Application Gateway listener configuration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/application-gateway/configuration-listeners)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Application Gateway named AppGW1 that load balances requests to a web app named App1.  
  
You need to modify the server variables in the response header of App1.  
  
What should you configure on AppGW1?
questions.explanation:
Azure Application Gateway (v2 SKU) provides a rewrite capability that lets you add, remove, or update HTTP headers, including using server variables (referenced with the var_ prefix) to build dynamic values for request or response headers. This functionality is configured through rewrite rule sets, which contain rewrite rules with conditions and actions applied to request/response headers or the URL. HTTP settings control backend pool behavior, listeners define how traffic is received, and rules link listeners to backend pools — none of these support server variable-based header rewriting, which is exclusively handled by the rewrites feature.

**Learn more:** [Rewrite HTTP headers and URL with Azure Application Gateway](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/application-gateway/rewrite-http-headers-url) · [Rewrite HTTP request and response headers in portal - Azure Application Gateway](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/application-gateway/rewrite-http-headers-portal)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an on-premises network named Site1.  
  
You have an Azure subscription that contains a storage account named storage1 and a virtual network named VNet1. VNet1 includes a subnet named Subnet1. A private endpoint for storage1 is connected to Subnet1. Site1 connects to VNet1 by using a Site-to-Site (S2S) VPN.  
  
You need to control access to storage1 from Site1 by using network security groups (NSGs).  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Configure a network policy for private endpoints on Subnet1.
Create a subnet delegation on Subnet1.
Associate a route table with Subnet1.
Associate a NAT gateway with Subnet1.

questions.explanation:
Azure disables private-endpoint network policies on a subnet by default. To apply NSG rules to traffic destined for a private endpoint, NSG support must first be enabled in the subnet's network policy for private endpoints.

**Learn more:** [Manage network policies for private endpoints - Azure Private Link](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/private-link/disable-private-endpoint-network-policy) · [What is a private endpoint? - Azure Private Link](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/private-link/private-endpoint-overview)

questions.domain: Design and implement Azure network security services
questions.question:
You must configure GW1 to satisfy the network-security requirements for P2S VPN users.  
  
Which tunnel type should you choose in GW1's Point-to-site configuration settings?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra ID authentication for Azure VPN Gateway point-to-site connections is supported only with the OpenVPN protocol. OpenVPN is SSL/TLS-based, so selecting **OpenVPN (SSL)** satisfies that authentication requirement.\
\
**Learn more:** [About Point-to-Site VPN connections - Azure VPN Gateway](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/point-to-site-about) · [Configure P2S VPN Gateway for Microsoft Entra ID authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/point-to-site-entra-gateway)

questions.question:
Solution: You deploy an Azure Front Door profile.  
  
Does this satisfy the requirement?
questions.explanation:
A secured Azure Virtual WAN hub requires an associated security provider and security/routing policies, such as Azure Firewall configured through Azure Firewall Manager. An Azure Front Door profile does not provide or configure the Virtual WAN hub security provider, so it does not change Hub1’s security status to Secured.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is a secured virtual hub?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall-manager/secured-virtual-hub) · [Configure Azure Firewall in a Virtual WAN hub](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-wan/howto-firewall)

questions.domain: Design and implement application delivery services
questions.question:
Solution: You deploy Azure Firewall.  
  
Does this satisfy the requirement?
questions.explanation:
Deploying Azure Firewall in an Azure Virtual WAN hub converts it to a secured hub, and the hub’s status is shown as **Secured**.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure Azure Firewall in a Virtual WAN hub](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-wan/howto-firewall)

questions.domain: Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.question:
Solution: You deploy Azure NAT Gateway.  
  
Does this satisfy the requirement?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Virtual WAN secured hub requires an integrated Azure Firewall or associated security and routing policies configured by Azure Firewall Manager. Azure NAT Gateway supplies outbound network address translation and does not convert a virtual WAN hub to a secured hub.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is a secured virtual hub?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall-manager/secured-virtual-hub) · [Configure Azure Firewall in a Virtual WAN hub](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-wan/howto-firewall)

questions.domain: Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.question:
Solution: You deploy Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF).  
  
Does this satisfy the requirement?
questions.explanation:
A secured Azure Virtual WAN hub is created by deploying Azure Firewall in the virtual hub. Azure Web Application Firewall is an application-layer web protection service and does not change a Virtual WAN hub’s security status to Secured.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure Azure Firewall in a Virtual WAN hub](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-wan/howto-firewall) · [What is a secured virtual hub?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall-manager/secured-virtual-hub)

questions.domain: Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.question:
Solution: You deploy Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF).  
  
Does this satisfy the requirement?
questions.explanation:
Azure Firewall Premium TLS inspection uses a trusted intermediate CA certificate to decrypt and re-encrypt outbound TLS traffic. The certificate must be stored in Azure Key Vault, and Azure Firewall uses a user-assigned managed identity with Key Vault secret permissions to retrieve it.

**Learn more:** [Azure Firewall Premium certificates](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall/premium-certificates)

You plan to deploy an Azure virtual network that will contain 10 virtual subnets. The subnets will use IPv6 addresses. Each subnet will host up to 200 load-balanced virtual machines.  
  
You need to recommend a load-balancing solution for the virtual network. The solution must satisfy the following requirements:  
  
- The virtual machines and the load balancer must be accessible only from the virtual network.  
- Costs must be minimized.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Standard Load Balancer can be configured as an internal load balancer with a private frontend IP from the virtual network, so its frontend is not exposed to the Internet. Azure Load Balancer supports IPv6 frontend IP configurations, and the Standard SKU provides the appropriate scalable Layer 4 load-balancing service for virtual machines without the additional Layer 7 gateway cost of Application Gateway.

**Learn more:** [Azure Load Balancer portal settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/load-balancer/manage) · [Overview of IPv6 for Azure Virtual Network](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/ip-services/ipv6-overview)

Subnet1 is associated with a service endpoint policy named Policy1. Policy1 defines one resource that references storage1.  
  
You deploy an Azure Batch pool named Pool1 to Subnet1.  
  
You need to ensure that the compute resources in Pool1 can access storage1.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: To Subnet1, add a storage endpoint for the storage service.
To Subnet1, add a subnet delegation.

questions.explanation:
An Azure Storage service endpoint must be enabled on the subnet for traffic from resources in that subnet to reach Azure Storage through the service endpoint. The service endpoint policy then filters that endpoint traffic and already allowlists storage1; it does not itself create the required endpoint.

**Learn more:** [Virtual network service endpoint policies for Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-service-endpoint-policies-overview) · [Azure Storage account with firewall causes errors when executing Batch jobs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/azure/hpc/batch/access-denied-execute-azure-batch-job)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that includes a virtual network named VNet1. VNet1 has a subnet named Subnet1.  
  
You deploy an Azure Application Gateway v2 instance named AppGw1 to Subnet1. You create a network security group (NSG) named NSG1 and associate NSG1 with Subnet1.  
  
You need to ensure that AppGw1 load balances only traffic originating from VNet1. The solution must minimize the effect on AppGw1 functionality.  
  
What should you add to NSG1?

options.text: an outbound rule that has a priority of 4096 and blocks all internet traffic
an inbound rule that has a priority of 4096 and blocks all internet traffic
an inbound rule that has a priority of 100 and blocks all internet traffic
an outbound rule that has a priority 100 and blocks all internet traffic

questions.explanation:
Azure Application Gateway v2 requires outbound connectivity to the Internet, so an outbound deny rule can disrupt gateway operation. An inbound rule that denies the `Internet` service tag at priority 4096 prevents Internet-sourced client traffic while leaving VirtualNetwork-sourced traffic eligible for the default `AllowVnetInBound` rule. Priority 4096 is the lowest custom-rule precedence, minimizing interference with more-specific required rules.

**Learn more:** [Azure Application Gateway infrastructure configuration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/application-gateway/configuration-infrastructure) · [Network security groups and application security groups](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/networking/design-guide/network-application-security-groups)

What should you include in the solution?

An Azure private endpoint provides private connectivity from a virtual network to an Azure Storage account through Azure Private Link. It assigns a private IP address from the virtual network to the storage service and keeps the connection on the Microsoft backbone, allowing public access to be restricted or disabled.\

A Site-to-Site VPN connection cannot be established between your company's main office and an Azure virtual network.  
  
You need to troubleshoot what is preventing the IPsec tunnel from being established. Which diagnostic log should you review?
questions.explanation:
IKEDiagnosticLog contains detailed IKE/IPsec negotiation and control-event data, making it the appropriate log for diagnosing failure to establish a Site-to-Site VPN IPsec tunnel. [Microsoft Learn: Troubleshoot Azure VPN Gateway using diagnostic logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/troubleshoot-vpn-with-azure-diagnostics)\
\
**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot Azure VPN Gateway using diagnostic logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/troubleshoot-vpn-with-azure-diagnostics)

questions.question:
Solution: You create a network security group (NSG) and associate it with Subnet1.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
An NSG association by itself does not limit outbound access to a particular Azure Storage account. NSG service tags can cover Azure Storage broadly or by region, not a single storage account. A virtual network service endpoint policy can allowlist an individual storage account and deny access to other storage accounts from the subnet.\
\
**Learn more:** [Virtual network service endpoint policies for Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-service-endpoint-policies-overview) · [Azure service tags overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/service-tags-overview)

questions.domain: Design and implement private access to Azure services
questions.question:
Solution: You configure the firewall on storage1 to accept connections only from Vnet1.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Storage network rules are configured per storage account. A rule on storage1 restricts access only to storage1; it does not prevent VM1 from accessing storage2 or storage3. Storage virtual-network rules also allow specific subnets, not an entire virtual network, and require the appropriate service endpoint. [Azure Storage firewall rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-network-security)\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Storage firewall rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-network-security)

questions.domain: Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.question:
Solution: Create a network security group (NSG), configure a service tag for Microsoft.Storage, and associate the tag with Subnet1.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Storage service tag represents Azure Storage IP address prefixes, not an individual storage account. An NSG rule using that tag can allow traffic to any storage account within the tag's scope; it cannot limit VM1 to only storage1. Azure service endpoint policies provide account-level filtering for Azure Storage egress over service endpoints.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure virtual network service endpoint policies for Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-service-endpoint-policies-overview) · [Azure service tags overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/service-tags-overview)

In Azure Application Gateway, path-based routing is implemented through routing rules. A rule associates a listener with one or more backend pools using a URL path map, so requests matching different paths (such as /app1, /app2) under the same hostname are routed to different backend pools/web apps. Listeners only define the frontend port, protocol, and hostname that the gateway listens on; HTTP settings define how traffic is sent to the backend (protocol, port, session affinity, probes); rewrites modify HTTP headers or the URL itself rather than determine routing destination. Therefore, controlling traffic flow based on URL path requires configuring a (path-based) rule.

**Learn more:** [URL path-based routing overview - Azure Application Gateway](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/application-gateway/url-route-overview) · [Application Gateway components](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/application-gateway/application-gateway-components)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have two Azure virtual networks named VNet1 and VNet2 that are peered to one another. VNet1 hosts 10 virtual machines containing web servers. VNet2 hosts five virtual machines containing database servers.  
  
You must configure a security solution that meets these requirements:  
  
- Ensures that the database servers accept connections only from the web servers  
- Ensures that the web servers can initiate connections only to the database servers  
- Ensures that all network security groups (NSGs) are associated only with subnets  
- Uses application security groups to implement the solution  
  
What is the minimum number of application security groups required?
questions.explanation:
An application security group (ASG) can only contain network interfaces from a single virtual network - all NICs assigned to an ASG must reside in the same VNet as the first NIC added. Because the web servers are in VNet1 and the database servers are in VNet2, you cannot place them in one shared ASG, so you need one ASG for the web servers (in VNet1) and one ASG for the database servers (in VNet2): a minimum of two. A single ASG (answer A) is impossible across the peered VNets, and four or eight are more than required. The NSGs are then associated to the subnets and use these two ASGs as source/destination to allow only web-to-database traffic.

**Learn more:** [Application security groups overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/application-security-groups)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains the following resources:  
  
- A virtual network named Vnet1  
- Two subnets named subnet1 and AzureFirewallSubnet  
- A public Azure Firewall named FW1  
- A route table named RT1 associated with Subnet1  
- A route in RT1 that sends `0.0.0.0/0` to FW1  
  
After deploying 10 servers running Windows Server to Subnet1, you find that none of the virtual machines have activated.  
  
You need to ensure that the virtual machines can be activated.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: On FW1, create an outbound service tag rule for AzureCloud.
Add an internet route to RT1 for the Azure Key Management Service (KMS).
On FW1, configure a DNAT rule for port 1688.
Deploy an Azure Standard Load Balancer that has an outbound NAT rule.

questions.explanation:
Azure Windows Server VMs use the Azure Key Management Service (KMS) endpoint on TCP port 1688 for activation. When a default route sends all traffic through a firewall, the subnet needs more-specific user-defined routes for the Azure KMS IP addresses with the Internet next hop. This permits KMS activation traffic to go directly to the Internet and override the `0.0.0.0/0` route.

**Learn more:** [Use Azure custom routes to enable KMS activation with forced tunneling](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/azure/virtual-machines/windows/custom-routes-enable-kms-activation) · [Event 8198 when activating Windows: KMS contact failure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/licensing-and-activation/activation-event-8198-error-0xc0020017-0x8007139f-kms-contact-failure)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has an office in New York.  
  
The company has an Azure subscription containing the virtual networks shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783826154617-pxz7p25b.png)  
  
You need to connect the virtual networks to the office by using ExpressRoute. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- The connection must support up to 1 Gbps of bandwidth.  
- The office must be able to access all the virtual networks.  
- Costs must be minimized.  
  
How many ExpressRoute circuits should be provisioned, and which ExpressRoute SKU should be enabled?
questions.explanation:
A single 1-Gbps ExpressRoute Premium circuit meets the bandwidth requirement and can be linked to multiple virtual networks. Premium extends ExpressRoute connectivity across geopolitical regions, which is required to reach the US and European virtual networks from the New York office; Standard does not support cross-geopolitical-region connectivity.

**Learn more:** [Azure ExpressRoute overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/expressroute/expressroute-introduction) · [Azure ExpressRoute FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/expressroute/expressroute-faqs)

Solution: You change the policy settings for WAF1.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:

\

questions.question:
Solution: Configure a custom rule for WAF1.  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Front Door WAF rate limiting is configured by using a custom WAF rule. A rate-limit custom rule evaluates matching incoming requests and enforces the configured request threshold; a WAF policy associated with the Front Door profile applies that rule to the profile's traffic.\
\

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure virtual network named Vnet1 with one subnet. Vnet1 is located in the West Europe region.  
  
You deploy an Azure App Service app named App1 in the West Europe region.  
  
You need to give App1 access to the resources in Vnet1. The solution must minimize costs.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Create a gateway subnet and deploy a virtual network gateway.

questions.explanation:
Azure App Service regional virtual network integration lets an app access resources in a virtual network in the same region and requires a dedicated, unused integration subnet. Creating a new subnet provides that prerequisite without the added cost of a virtual network gateway or other unnecessary networking services.

**Learn more:** [Integrate your app with an Azure virtual network - Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-vnet-integration) · [Enable virtual network integration in Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/configure-vnet-integration-enable)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has four branch offices and an Azure subscription. The subscription includes an Azure VPN gateway named GW1.  
  
The branch offices are configured as shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783826145215-j4olbhk5.png)  
  
The branch-office routers provide internet connectivity and Site-to-Site VPN connections to GW1.  
  
Users in Branch1 report that they can connect to internet resources but cannot access Azure resources.  
  
You need to ensure that Branch1 users can connect to the Azure resources. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
- Minimize downtime for all users.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do first?
questions.explanation:
Resetting the specific Site-to-Site VPN connection, Connection1, resets and restores only that selected connection; it does not reboot the Azure VPN gateway. This confines disruption to the affected Branch1 tunnel and avoids interrupting the other branch connections, while requiring less effort than recreating the local network gateway.

**Learn more:** [Reset a VPN gateway or a connection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/reset-gateway)

You have an Azure subscription containing a virtual network named VNet1 and a storage account named storage1.  
  
Site1 and VNet1 are connected by using a Site-to-Site (S2S) VPN.  
  
You need to ensure that the servers in Site1 can connect to storage1 by using the S2S VPN. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you create in VNet1?
questions.explanation:
An Azure private endpoint creates a network interface with a private IP address in VNet1 for the storage account. On-premises clients connected to the virtual network through an S2S VPN can access Azure Storage through that private endpoint, avoiding public-internet access. Service endpoints apply to traffic originating from VNet subnets and do not provide this on-premises private-access path.

**Learn more:** [Use private endpoints for Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-private-endpoints) · [What is Azure Private Link?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/private-link/private-link-overview)

You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to implement Azure Virtual WAN as shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783826234273-69ujtjfk.png)  
  
What is the minimum number of route tables that you need to create?
questions.explanation:
Each Azure Virtual WAN virtual hub has its own Default route table, and connections associate with and propagate to that table by default. Because the deployment contains two virtual hubs and requires no separate routing or isolation policy, two route tables are sufficient.\
\
**Learn more:** [About virtual hub routing - Azure Virtual WAN](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-wan/about-virtual-hub-routing)

questions.domain: Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.question:
You are designing the IP addressing for subnets in Azure virtual networks.  
  
Which resource type requires IP addresses within the subnets?
questions.explanation:
An internal load balancer uses a private frontend IP address selected from the virtual network subnet. Therefore, it requires an IP address in that subnet.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Load Balancer portal settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/load-balancer/manage)

questions.domain: Design and implement Azure network security services
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are setting up two network virtual appliances (NVAs) in an Azure virtual network. The NVAs will inspect all traffic within the virtual network.  
  
You need to ensure high availability for the NVAs while minimizing administrative effort.  
  
What should the solution include?
questions.explanation:
Azure Standard Load Balancer provides Layer 4 load balancing and health probes for NVA instances. Its HA Ports rules can load-balance all TCP and UDP ports to healthy NVAs, making it suitable for highly available inspection of virtual-network traffic with minimal administrative overhead.

**Learn more:** [Deploy highly available NVAs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/networking/guide/network-virtual-appliance-high-availability) · [Azure Load Balancer components](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/load-balancer/components)

You have an on-premises datacenter in Seattle.  
  
You have an Azure subscription that includes an Azure Network Watcher resource in the West US 2 Azure region.  
  
You need to document network latency between the on-premises datacenter and the West US 2 region, as well as between the on-premises datacenter and the East US 2 public Azure region. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Create a Network Watcher resource in the East US 2 region.
Create a Connection Monitor resource in the West US 2 region.

questions.explanation:
Azure Network Watcher Connection Monitor provides continuous connectivity monitoring and records latency metrics for hybrid environments. A Connection Monitor is a regional resource and can use on-premises machines as sources while monitoring Azure or public endpoints, so creating it in the existing West US 2 region avoids deploying an additional Network Watcher resource in East US 2.

**Learn more:** [Connection monitor overview — Azure Network Watcher](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/connection-monitor-overview) · [Create a connection monitor — Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/connection-monitor-create-using-portal)

questions.domain: Design and implement core networking infrastructure
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that includes a virtual network named VNet1.  
  
You plan to deploy Point-to-Site (P2S) VPN access for VNet1.  
  
You need to recommend an authentication method for the deployment. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Require use of a FIDO2 security key.  
- Analyze user sign-in behavior.  
- Require a user to change their password when their sign-in behavior is identified as risky.  
  
What should you recommend?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra ID authentication for P2S VPN supports Conditional Access, which can enforce an authentication strength requiring a FIDO2 security key. Microsoft Entra ID Protection analyzes sign-in and user risk, and a user-risk policy can require risk remediation; users with passwords are prompted to perform a secure password change after multifactor authentication. Azure VPN Gateway supports Microsoft Entra ID as a P2S authentication method.

**Learn more:** [About Azure Point-to-Site VPN connections](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/point-to-site-about) · [Configure and enable risk policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-protection/howto-identity-protection-configure-risk-policies)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783885398077-xeqyfd8d.png)  
  
You need to configure a solution that meets these requirements:  
  
- App1 must have a private endpoint assigned.  
- Internet access to App1 must be routed through FD1.  
  
What should you configure on FD1?

options.text: a security policy that redirects traffic
a rule that has the route configuration override action
an origin that enables the Azure Private Link service

questions.explanation:
Azure Front Door Premium supports Private Link for an Azure App Service origin. Enabling the Azure Private Link service on the origin creates a private endpoint connection from Azure Front Door’s managed network to the web app; internet clients can still access the application through the Front Door endpoint. Redirect and route-override settings only alter request routing behavior and do not create private connectivity to the origin.

**Learn more:** [Secure your origin with Private Link in Azure Front Door Premium](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/frontdoor/private-link) · [How to configure an origin for Azure Front Door](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/frontdoor/how-to-configure-origin)

questions.domain: Design and implement Azure network security services
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have two Azure subscriptions, **Sub1** and **Sub2**. **Sub1** contains a virtual machine named **VM1**.  
  
You plan to use Azure Private Link to make **VM1** available to resources in **Sub2**.  
  
You need to ensure that the private link service can be configured to provide access to **VM1**.  
  
What should you configure in **Sub1** first?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Private Link service exposes a customer-owned service that is deployed behind an Azure Standard Load Balancer. Configuring VM1 as a backend of the load balancer provides the required frontend configuration to which the Private Link service attaches.

**Learn more:** [What is Azure Private Link?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/private-link/private-link-overview) · [Quickstart: Create a Private Link service by using the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/private-link/create-private-link-service-portal)

questions.domain: Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have the resources displayed in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783886591717-iaue5kqm.png)  
  
You need to protect the virtual machines by using Azure DDoS Network Protection plans.  
  
What is the minimum number of DDoS Network Protection plans that you should deploy?
questions.explanation:
One Azure DDoS Network Protection plan can protect linked virtual networks across multiple subscriptions within the same Microsoft Entra tenant. Because Sub1, Sub2, and Sub3 are all linked to Tenant1, a single plan is sufficient; the management group and the number of virtual machines do not require additional plans.

**Learn more:** [Azure DDoS Protection overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ddos-protection/ddos-protection-overview) · [Manage DDoS Protection plans: permissions and restrictions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ddos-protection/manage-permissions)

questions.domain: Design and implement Azure network security services
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has a remote office containing a macOS device named Device1. Device1 has an IKEv2 VPN client installed.  
  
You have an Azure subscription that contains the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783884329375-6njpsnbz.png)  
  
You need to ensure that Device1 can access the resources on VNet1 by using VPNGW1 VPN connections. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: To VNet1, deploy a virtual machine that contains a RADIUS server.
On Device1, install the OpenVPN client.
On Device1, add an X.509 certificate.
From Devices in the Microsoft Entra admin center, configure the Device settings.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra ID authentication for Azure VPN Gateway point-to-site connections is supported only through the OpenVPN protocol, not IKEv2. Installing an OpenVPN-compatible client on the macOS device enables it to use the required authentication method without deploying and administering a RADIUS server or switching to certificate-based authentication.

**Learn more:** [About Azure Point-to-Site VPN connections](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/point-to-site-about) · [Configure P2S VPN Gateway for Microsoft Entra ID authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/point-to-site-entra-gateway)
