questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription containing a virtual network named Vnet1. Vnet1 includes a virtual machine named VM1 and an Azure firewall named FW1.  
  
An Azure Firewall Policy named FP1 is associated with FW1.  
  
You need to ensure that RDP requests sent to FW1's public IP address are routed to VM1.  
  
What should you configure on FP1?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Firewall Policy DNAT rule translates inbound traffic addressed to the firewall’s public IP address and port to a virtual machine’s private IP address and port. Configuring a DNAT rule for TCP port 3389 publishes RDP access to VM1 through FW1.\
\
**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Filter inbound Internet traffic with Azure Firewall policy DNAT using the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall/tutorial-firewall-dnat-policy)

questions.domain: Design and implement application delivery services

options.text: Modify the rate limit threshold of Rule1.
Modify the rule type of Rule1.

questions.explanation:
Azure Front Door WAF rate-limit rules apply their request threshold separately to each source IP address. An IP match condition can contain multiple IP addresses or ranges, evaluated with OR logic. Adding the Seattle and Paris public IP addresses to Rule1’s conditions causes the existing 100-request rate limit to apply independently to all three office IP addresses.

**Learn more:** [Web application firewall rate limiting for Azure Front Door](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/web-application-firewall/afds/waf-front-door-rate-limit) · [Configure Azure Front Door rules match conditions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/frontdoor/rules-match-conditions)

questions.domain: Design and implement application delivery services
questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that contains a virtual network named VNet1. VNet1 includes a subnet named Subnet1.  
  
You plan to add a private endpoint to Subnet.  
  
You need to ensure that traffic can be routed between the private endpoint and the Azure Private Link service by using a user-defined route.  
  
What should you do first on Subnet1?

options.text: Provision a Standard Azure load balancer.

questions.explanation:
Private endpoint network policies must be enabled on the subnet to use user-defined routes with a private endpoint. Azure disables these policies by default for private endpoint subnets; enabling them permits route-table support.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage network policies for private endpoints - Azure Private Link](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/private-link/disable-private-endpoint-network-policy)

questions.domain: Design and implement private access to Azure services
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has an on-premises network and three Azure subscriptions named Subscription1, Subscription2, and Subscription3.  
  
The company departments use the Azure subscriptions as shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783807901237-q0v92u05.png)  
  
All resources in the subscriptions are located in either the West US Azure region or the West US 2 Azure region.  
  
You plan to connect every subscription to the on-premises network by using ExpressRoute.  
  
What is the minimum number of ExpressRoute circuits required?
questions.explanation:
One ExpressRoute circuit can link virtual networks across multiple Azure subscriptions, with the circuit bandwidth shared by those virtual networks. The West US and West US 2 regions are in the same geopolitical region, so a single circuit can serve the subscriptions without requiring an additional circuit for regional scope.

**Learn more:** [FAQ - Azure ExpressRoute](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/expressroute/expressroute-faqs)

You have an Azure subscription containing a Basic Azure virtual WAN. The virtual WAN has one virtual hub and a virtual network gateway limited to 1 Gbps of throughput.

You need to connect Vnet2 and Vnet3. The solution must satisfy the virtual networking requirements and the business requirements.  
  
Which two actions should you include in the solution? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: On the peering from Vnet1, select Allow for Traffic forwarded from remote virtual network.
On the peerings from Vnet2 and Vnet3, select Allow for Traffic forwarded from remote virtual network.
On the peering from Vnet1, select Use the remote virtual network's gateway or Route Server.
On the peering from Vnet1, select Allow for Traffic to remote virtual network.
On the peerings from Vnet2 and Vnet3, select Use the remote virtual network's gateway or Route Server.

questions.explanation:
Vnet1 is the transit hub for the ExpressRoute connection. Its peerings must allow forwarded traffic so traffic can traverse the hub, and Vnet2 and Vnet3 must be configured to use Vnet1's remote gateway to share the hub gateway for connectivity to Boston. This provides the required routed hub-and-spoke path without deploying separate gateways in the spoke virtual networks.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot virtual network peering issues](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-troubleshoot-peering-issues) · [Azure Virtual Network peering overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-peering-overview)

questions.question:
You have 10 Azure App Service instances. Each instance hosts the same web app, and every instance is located in a different Azure region.  
  
You need to configure Azure Traffic Manager to route users to the instance with the lowest latency.  
  
Which routing method should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Traffic Manager Performance routing directs a user to the available endpoint that provides the lowest network latency from that user's network. It is designed for endpoints deployed in different geographic regions.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure performance traffic routing method using Azure Traffic Manager](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/traffic-manager/traffic-manager-configure-performance-routing-method)

questions.question:
You are planning IP addressing for subnets in Azure virtual networks.  
  
Which resource type requires IP addresses from the subnets?
questions.explanation:
A private endpoint creates a network interface in the selected subnet and receives a private IP address from that subnet’s address range. [Microsoft Learn: What is a private endpoint?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/private-link/private-endpoint-overview)\
\
**Learn more:** [What is a private endpoint? - Azure Private Link](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/private-link/private-endpoint-overview)

questions.question:
You are planning IP addressing for subnets in Azure virtual networks.  
  
Which resource type requires IP addresses from the subnets?

options.text: peering links between Vnet1 and Vnet2
a route table associated to Subnet1-1 and Subnet2-1
a route table associated to AzureFirewallSubnet

questions.explanation:
Azure Firewall can inspect traffic between peered spoke virtual networks only when user-defined routes on the spoke workload subnets send the destination subnet prefix to the firewall’s private IP address with a virtual-appliance next hop. Associating a route table with both Subnet1-1 and Subnet2-1 enforces the firewall path in both directions; the AzureFirewallSubnet itself generally relies on system routes to reach peered networks.

**Learn more:** [Azure Firewall and traffic inspection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/networking/design-guide/azure-firewall) · [Azure Firewall FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall/firewall-faq)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing a distributed web app named App1. App1 is hosted in multiple Azure regions.  
  
You need to recommend a solution to route user requests to App. The solution must satisfy these requirements:  
  
- Support routing a user request to a resource based on the request URL.  
- Support query string replacement.  
- Minimize network latency.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Azure Front Door provides URL-path-based route matching and rule sets that can rewrite or redirect URLs, including replacing query strings. Its global edge network and latency routing send requests to the appropriate origin with the lowest network latency.

**Learn more:** [How requests get matched to a route configuration - Azure Front Door](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/frontdoor/front-door-route-matching) · [URL Redirect - Azure Front Door](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/frontdoor/front-door-url-redirect)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure virtual network named Vnet1.  
  
You need to ensure that the virtual machines in Vnet1 can access only Azure SQL resources in the East US Azure region. The virtual machines must be prevented from accessing any Azure Storage resources.  
  
Which two outbound network security group (NSG) rules should you create? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: a deny rule that has a source of VirtualNetwork and a destination of Sql
an allow rule that has the IP address range of Vnet1 as the source and destination of Sql.EastUS
a deny rule that has a source of VirtualNetwork and a destination of 168.63.129.0/24
a deny rule that has the IP address range of Vnet1 as the source and destination of Storage

questions.explanation:
The `Sql.EastUS` service tag scopes an outbound rule to Azure SQL service address prefixes in East US. The `Storage` service tag represents Azure Storage address space, so an outbound deny rule to that tag prevents access to Azure Storage resources. Service tags are Microsoft-managed address-prefix groups and support regional variants for both SQL and Storage. [Azure service tags overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/service-tags-overview)

**Learn more:** [Azure service tags overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/service-tags-overview) · [Network security groups and application security groups](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/networking/design-guide/network-application-security-groups)

questions.explanation:
Traffic Analytics analyzes Network Watcher flow logs, which are stored in an Azure Storage account, and uses a Log Analytics workspace to store and analyze the resulting Azure Monitor log data. options.text: Add a network interface to VMSS1.
Add a public IP address to each member of VMSS1.

questions.explanation:
An Azure Load Balancer load-balancing rule defines the frontend-to-backend mapping and distributes incoming traffic to instances in its backend pool. A health probe determines which backend instances are healthy and therefore eligible to receive new traffic. VMSS1's instances are already in the backend pool, and they do not need individual public IP addresses for inbound load balancing.

**Learn more:** [Azure Load Balancer components](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/load-balancer/components) · [Azure Load Balancer health probes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/load-balancer/load-balancer-custom-probe-overview)

You have the Azure environment displayed in the exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783795617915-qprmo5p5.png)  
  
VM1 is a virtual machine with an instance-level public IP address (ILPIP). Basic Load Balancer uses a public IP address, and VM1 and VM2 are members of its backend pool. NAT Gateway uses a public IP address named IP3 that is associated with SubnetA. VNet1 has a virtual network gateway with a public IP address named IP4.  
  
When VM1 initiates outbound traffic to the internet, which public address is used?
questions.explanation:
An Azure NAT Gateway associated with a subnet provides the preferred outbound internet connectivity for resources in that subnet. It takes precedence over instance-level public IP addresses and Load Balancer outbound connectivity for new outbound connections, so VM1's traffic is source-NATed to IP3.

**Learn more:** [What is Azure NAT Gateway?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/nat-gateway/nat-overview) · [Design virtual networks with Azure NAT Gateway](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/nat-gateway/nat-gateway-design)

questions.domain: Design and implement private access to Azure services
questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You need to deploy an App Service web app named App1 that uses an Azure application gateway. App1 is estimated to use 250,000 persistent connections.  
  
What is the minimum number of app instances that you should configure?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Application Gateway capacity unit supports 2,500 persistent connections, and each instance guarantees 10 capacity units. Each instance therefore supports 25,000 persistent connections; 250,000 required connections need 10 instances.\
\
**Learn more:** [Understanding pricing - Azure Application Gateway](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/application-gateway/understanding-pricing)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has offices in New York and Amsterdam and an Azure subscription. Both offices connect to Azure by using Site-to-Site VPN connections.  
  
The Amsterdam office uses resources in the North Europe Azure region. The New York office uses resources in the East US Azure region.  
  
You need to implement ExpressRoute circuits that connect each office to its nearest Azure region. After the ExpressRoute circuits are connected, on-premises computers in the Amsterdam office must be able to connect to on-premises servers in the New York office by using the ExpressRoute circuits.  
  
Which ExpressRoute option should you use?
questions.explanation:
ExpressRoute Global Reach links ExpressRoute circuits to create private connectivity between the on-premises networks attached to them, with cross-site traffic traversing the Microsoft global network.

**Learn more:** [About Azure ExpressRoute Global Reach](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/expressroute/expressroute-global-reach) · [Azure ExpressRoute overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/expressroute/expressroute-introduction)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783828996443-yu8lv4q7.png)  
  
You must ensure that VM1 and VM2 can connect only to storage1. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Prevent VM1 and VM2 from accessing any other storage accounts.  
- Ensure that storage1 remains accessible from the internet.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
A service endpoint policy applied to Subnet1 can allowlist storage1 and deny VM1 and VM2 access to every other Azure Storage account over the service endpoint. It controls outbound traffic from the subnet without requiring storage1 to use a private-only endpoint, so the storage account can remain accessible through its public internet endpoint.

**Learn more:** [Azure virtual network service endpoint policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-service-endpoint-policies-overview) · [Create and associate service endpoint policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-service-endpoint-policies)

questions.domain: Design and implement application delivery services
questions.question:
You plan to deploy an Azure virtual network that will contain 10 virtual subnets. The subnets will use IPv6 addresses. Each subnet will host up to 200 load-balanced virtual machines.  
  
You need to recommend the subnet mask size to use for the virtual subnets.  
  
What should you recommend?
questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Network requires every IPv6 subnet to use an exact `/64` prefix. A `/64` provides sufficient address capacity for 200 load-balanced virtual machines; `/120`, `/48`, and `/24` are not valid IPv6 subnet sizes for this Azure requirement.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Virtual Network FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-networks-faq) · [Plan for IP addressing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/ready/azure-best-practices/plan-for-ip-addressing)

You are planning IP addressing for subnets in Azure virtual networks.  
  
Which resource type requires IP addresses within the subnets?
questions.explanation:
An internal load balancer requires a private frontend IP address selected from a virtual network subnet. This consumes an address in that subnet. [Azure Load Balancer portal settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/load-balancer/manage)\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Load Balancer portal settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/load-balancer/manage)

Remove the existing virtual network peerings.

questions.explanation:
In an Azure Virtual WAN migration, spoke virtual networks are disconnected from the former customer-managed hub by deleting their hub peerings, and they connect to the Virtual WAN hub by using virtual network connections. The old hub can become a shared-services spoke that continues to host Azure Application Gateway for centralized internet ingress. Routing previously implemented for the customer-managed hub-and-spoke design must be replaced for the Virtual WAN topology.

**Learn more:** [Architecture: Migrate to Azure Virtual WAN](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-wan/migrate-from-hub-spoke-topology) · [Connect a virtual network to a Virtual WAN hub](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-wan/howto-connect-vnet-hub)

questions.domain: Design, implement, and manage connectivity services
questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that includes an Azure Firewall Standard instance named AzFW1.  
  
You plan to enable the following:  
  
- TLS inspection  
- Threat intelligence  
- A network intrusion detection and prevention system (IDPS)  
  
What can you enable by using AzFW1?

options.text: TLS inspection and the IDPS only
threat intelligence and the IDPS only
TLS inspection, threat intelligence, and the IDPS

questions.explanation:
Azure Firewall Standard supports threat intelligence-based filtering. TLS inspection and IDPS are available only with the Azure Firewall Premium SKU, so an Azure Firewall Standard instance can enable threat intelligence only.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Firewall features by SKU](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall/features-by-sku) · [Choose the right Azure Firewall SKU to meet your needs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall/choose-firewall-sku)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783885153356-q86rhgcv.png)  
  
VNet1 contains a subnet named Subnet.  
  
You need to ensure that resources connected to Subnet1 can access only storage1 and storage3. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
Which configuration should you use?
questions.explanation:
A service endpoint policy is associated with a subnet and allowlists specific Azure Storage accounts by resource ID for traffic over service endpoints. Once applied, only the storage accounts listed in the policy are accessible from that subnet, so storage1 and storage3 can be allowed while storage2 is denied.

**Learn more:** [Azure virtual network service endpoint policies for Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-service-endpoint-policies-overview)

questions.domain: Design and implement application delivery services
questions.question: What should be implemented to satisfy the virtual-network requirements for the virtual machines that connect to Vnet4 and Vnet5?
questions.explanation:
Azure virtual network peering creates private connectivity between two virtual networks, allowing virtual machines and other resources in the peered networks to communicate over the Microsoft backbone. A route table alone cannot establish that connectivity, while service endpoints, private endpoints, and Private Link Service address access to services rather than general VNet-to-VNet communication.\
\
**Learn more:** [Virtual network peering](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-peering-overview)
